draft.title: Environmental factors in farming
card: Environmental factors are natural conditions that affect what a farm can grow. The four main ones are climate, soil, landform and water.
Climate is the usual pattern of temperature and rainfall. Crops need enough warmth and water, from rain or from rivers and groundwater, to grow well.
Deep, fertile soil holds nutrients and moisture for roots. Flat land is easier to plough and water than steep slopes, where soil can wash away.
Wheat suits Australia's dry plains because it grows with modest rain. Rice suits the wet river deltas of Asia because it grows best in flooded, water-rich fields.
draft.remember: Natural conditions help decide which crops suit a place.

a.q: Why is rice grown on the wet river deltas of Asia?
opts: It grows best where water is plentiful and land is flat
It grows best where rain is low and soils are thin
It grows best on steep slopes with fast drainage
It grows best where the climate is cool and dry
a.why: Rice needs a lot of water, and river deltas are flat and wet. Dry conditions and steep slopes suit it poorly, so the option about low rain is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what rice needs from the land and water.

b.q: Tom wants to farm wheat in a district with little rain. Which natural condition best suits wheat?
opts: Flat plains with modest rainfall
Flooded fields with heavy rainfall
Steep hills with thin, stony soil
Cold land that is frozen all year
b.why: The card says wheat suits dry plains because it grows with modest rain, and flat land is easy to work. Flooded fields suit rice, not wheat.
b.clue: Wheat is the crop of Australia's dry plains.

a.best: It grows best where water is plentiful and land is flat

problems.detail: The clue 'Wheat is the crop of Australia's dry plains' points straight at the only option that mentions plains. A student can pick it by matching words without understanding what wheat needs.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate. The one problem is question b's clue: it names 'plains', which gives away the right option, so it should be reworded to prompt thinking about how much water wheat needs.

a.q: Why does rice suit the river deltas of Asia?
opts: It grows best where water is plentiful and land is flat
It grows best where rain is low and soils are thin
It grows best on steep slopes with fast drainage
It grows best where the climate is cool and dry
a.why: Rice grows best in flooded fields, and river deltas are flat and full of water. Low rain and thin soil describe a dry place, which suits rice poorly.
a.clue: Think about how much water rice fields hold.

b.q: Tom farms a flat plain with modest rainfall and no river to flood his fields. Which crop suits his farm, and why?
opts: Wheat, because it grows well with modest rain
Rice, because it grows best in flooded fields
Rice, because flat land is easy to plough and water
Wheat, because it grows best in flooded fields
b.why: Wheat grows with modest rain, which matches Tom's farm. Flat land does help rice, but rice grows best in flooded fields, and Tom has no water to flood them.
b.clue: How much water can Tom's fields get?
